name: PureMails
author: purehost

sections.description:
PureMails is a transactional email service sending from Germany. This plugin connects your WordPress website to it.

  • One-key setup. Paste an API key from the PureMails customer portal; the plugin creates its own SMTP login and picks a verified sender address.
  • All emails of the website. Contact forms, orders, password resets and newsletters sent with wp_mail() go through PureMails, encrypted and authenticated.
  • Bounces back into your newsletter tool. Every 15 minutes the plugin fetches bounces and complaints and marks the addresses in MailPoet, The Newsletter Plugin, FluentCRM, Groundhogg, Icegram Express (Email Subscribers & Newsletters), Noptin and AcyMailing: hard bounces and complaints right away, soft bounces after three within 30 days (configurable). Other tools can use the sendmails_ereignis action.
  • Email log with delivery status. Every email with recipient, subject, the plugin that sent it and its real status at the recipient: delivered, hard or soft bounce with the server response, complaint. Search, filters and, optionally, “Send again”.
  • Quota and rates in the dashboard. Monthly quota with forecast, bounce and complaint rate, sending rate and limits, deliveries per day, bounces by provider and reason.
  • Protection against abused forms. If a plugin or theme suddenly sends far more emails than usual, for example because bots flood a contact form, further emails from that source are held until you decide: send, discard or always trust the source.
  • Warnings before your customers notice. Email to the administrator when the quota reaches 80 or 100 %, the bounce or complaint rate approaches the limit, emails are held or stuck in the queue, or the sender domain is no longer verified. Plus a short weekly report on Mondays.
  • Safe during disruptions. If PureMails is briefly unreachable, emails wait in a local queue and are retried for up to 24 hours. The plugin switches between the PureMails mail servers automatically.
  • Domain check, Site Health and WP-CLI. DNS status of every sender domain with copy buttons, tests in Site Health and wp sendmails commands for agencies.
  • Guided setup with test email and a self-test against two test mailboxes (delivery and bounce).

No open or click tracking. Recipients and subjects stay in the email log for 30 days by default (configurable, or not at all); email content only if you turn it on, for at most 7 days. Credentials are stored encrypted in the database or as constants in wp-config.php.

The plugin requires a PureMails account. Plans and ordering: PureMails.

The user interface is in English; translations are provided through translate.wordpress.org.

External services

This plugin connects to services operated by PureHost (PureMails), the email service it is made for. It does not work without them.

  • Mail sending (smtp.send-mails.de): every email sent by WordPress after you turn on sending, including recipients, subject, content and attachments, is transmitted via SMTP (TLS, authenticated with your SMTP login) to the mail servers of PureMails for delivery. The plugin only connects to mail servers under PureMails. The test email and the self-test send emails only when you start them.
  • API (api.send-mails.de): authenticated with your API key. When you save the key and during setup, the plugin sends the address of your website to create an SMTP login for it. Every 15 minutes and when you open the plugin pages, it retrieves your quota, statistics, verified domains, the mail servers to use, new bounce and complaint events (these contain the affected recipient addresses) and the delivery status of recently sent emails (identified by a random ID per email).
  • Customer portal (portal.send-mails.de): the plugin pages only link to the portal. Nothing is transmitted unless you open a link yourself.

Terms of service: https://www.pure-mails.de/agb.html
Privacy policy: https://www.pure-mails.de/datenschutz.html

Developers

  • do_action('sendmails_ereignis', $wirkung, $email, $ereignis): $wirkung is bounced or beschwerde (complaint).
  • apply_filters('sendmails_ref', $ref): content of the X-SendMails-Ref header.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. In the customer portal of PureMails, create an API key with the purpose “WordPress plugin”.
  3. Open “PureMails” in the WordPress admin menu and follow the steps: API key, SMTP login (set up automatically), sender, test email, turn on sending.

Instead of the database, credentials can be stored in wp-config.php:

define('SENDMAILS_SMTP_BENUTZER', '...');
define('SENDMAILS_SMTP_PASSWORT', '...');
define('SENDMAILS_API_SCHLUESSEL', 'sm_live_...');

WP-Cron runs on page views. On low-traffic sites a real cron job for wp-cron.php is recommended.
sections.faq:
Do I need a PureMails account?

Yes. The plugin sends through PureMails and needs an API key or an SMTP login from the customer portal.

Does it work with other SMTP plugins?

It replaces them. Another plugin that takes over email sending (WP Mail SMTP, FluentSMTP, Post SMTP, Easy WP SMTP and others) is detected; for the common ones, “Switch now” takes over the sender, deactivates the old plugin (its settings stay) and turns on sending.

What happens if PureMails is unreachable?

Emails wait in a local queue and are sent again for up to 24 hours. Nothing is sent twice.

Can I see whether an email has arrived?

Yes. The email log shows every email with recipient, subject, the plugin that sent it and its status at the recipient (delivered, bounced with the server response, complaint). Recipients and subjects are kept for 30 days by default, or not at all if you choose so.

What if a contact form is flooded by bots?

If a plugin or theme suddenly sends far more emails than usual, further emails from it are held and the administrator gets an email. You decide whether to send or discard them. Newsletter tools are never held.

What happens when the monthly quota is used up?

You choose in the settings: stop sending, continue at a reduced pace, or continue normally. In the last two cases the overage is charged up to a cost cap you set, only after you have agreed to it.

Does the plugin track opens or clicks?

No.

Is there WP-CLI support?

Yes: wp sendmails status, test, abgleich, warteschlange, protokoll and bremse.
sections.changelog:
1.0.9

  • New name: PureMails. Logo, display name and all texts use the new name; the website is now www.pure-mails.de. Sending, API, settings and data are unchanged (smtp.send-mails.de, api.send-mails.de).

1.0.8

  • New look in the PureHost design: logo, colours and typography match www.send-mails.de.
  • Display name is now PureHost SendMails; the service is called SendMails in all texts (slug, settings and data unchanged).

1.0.7

  • New name: PureHost Send-Mails (slug purehost-send-mails).
  • Translations are delivered through translate.wordpress.org; no bundled language files.
  • Input from $_SERVER sanitized in the Newsletter adapter.

1.0.6

  • Text domain and folder name are now “send-mails”, matching the plugin slug on WordPress.org.

1.0.5

  • Readme: external services described by their public addresses only.

1.0.4

  • New name: Send-Mails.
  • Changelog of the versions before 1.0 moved to changelog.txt.

1.0.3

  • Sender settings: the domain next to the @ is no longer cut off.

1.0.2

  • Placeholders of the email log query passed one by one (Plugin Check).

1.0.1

  • Code review for the WordPress.org directory: stricter input sanitising, fixed queries with placeholders for the email log filters.

1.0.0

  • First stable release: email log with delivery status, protection against mass sending, warnings and weekly report, choice when the quota is used up, domain check, sender per source, email design, Site Health, WP-CLI and switching from other SMTP plugins in one click.
  • Settings in separate tiles with a jump bar (Connection, Sender, Quota, Protection and warnings, Email log, Bounces and queue, WordPress notifications, Email design); the email log has its own form.
  • Every sentence of a hint text starts on its own line; long sentences were shortened.

Older versions: see changelog.txt in the plugin folder.
